intent: The button whose hover or keyboard focus opens its Tooltip's hint.
typical_uses: The control a Tooltip describes, such as an icon-only toolbar button

dont_use_when.situation: A button with no hint attached to it

invariants.text: `disabled` stops this trigger from opening the tooltip and stamps `data-trigger-disabled`; it does not set the native `disabled` attribute, so the button stays focusable and clickable.
Hovering opens the tooltip for mouse pointers only, after the pointer rests on the trigger for the open delay; keyboard focus on the trigger opens it as well.

anti_patterns.dont: Pass `disabled` to make the button itself inert
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use `disabled` only to suppress the tooltip; to disable the element, give the rendered element its own native `disabled` through `render`, as the primitive's own prop documentation directs

a11y.by: the primitive's Tooltip.Trigger renders a native button; tooltip.test.tsx asserts getByRole('button', { name: 'Hover me' }) on it and that focusing it opens the tooltip ("opens on trigger focus")

handle.states: handle is an opaque object from the primitive's Tooltip.createHandle(), tying this trigger to a Tooltip root it is not placed inside
handle.because: `TooltipHandle<Payload>` is a class instance holding the tooltip's store, not data; the kit re-exports no createHandle, so a caller imports it from the primitive.

payload.states: payload is any value handed to the root's function children when this trigger opens the tooltip
payload.because: Typed by the caller's own `Payload` type parameter (`unknown` here), so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the trigger's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the trigger's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through tooltip.module.css, not through this.

good.title: The kit's Button rendered as the trigger
A trigger that opens sooner than the default

bad.title: A kit Button nested inside the trigger
bad.why: The trigger already renders a native button, so this nests a button inside a button, which HTML does not allow; pass the Button through `render` instead.
